## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Yakkhapahāra Sutta* (Ud 4.4, PTS Ud 39) is a discourse in the *Udāna* collection of the Pali Canon. The text recounts an episode in which a spirit (*yakkha*) delivers a violent blow to the head of the Venerable Sāriputta while he sits in meditation.

Full parallels to the sutta are preserved in the Chinese Āgamas, specifically two *Saṁyuktāgama* versions: SA 1330 and SA2 329 (both titled 害及無害), alongside a resembling parallel in the *Ekottarikāgama* (EA 48.6).

Within Pali literature, the sutta is cited or referenced in the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37), the *Peṭakopadesa* (Pe 2, Pe 8), and the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.1.1).

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
